When he insisted on separate consoles, she got upset, called him names, and stormed out. He's asking if he's the asshole.

Hmm... I need to recall how Animal Crossing works technically. The key point is: " you can only have one village per Nintendo Switch console." That's correct. Each Switch console can only have one Animal Crossing save file per user account. But if you have two Switches, you can each have your own separate saves on your own consoles. 

The girlfriend's request: "share one village" on one Switch. But if they're both using one Switch, they'd have to share the same save file. That means they'd both be playing in the same town, same island, same everything. They'd have to coordinate schedules, and neither could customize their own space independently. 

The user's stance: He wants each to have their own copy of the game (so two Switches, two saves) so they can play online separately but still visit each其他's islands. That's actually the standard way to play Animal Crossing with a partner - each has their own island, then you can互相 visit. 

Why is this important? Because in Animal Crossing, the "village" ( island) is tied to the save file. If they share one save file on one Switch, they're literally sharing the same physical space. That means: 
- They'd both be on the same island at the same time ( unless one is offline, but then the other would be alone in the shared space)
- They'd have to agree on every design choice, every tree cut, every flower arrangement 
- They couldn't have different themes or styles 
- If one person wants to move their house or change the layout, the other has to live with it 

Whereas if each has their own Switch and game copy: 
- They each have their own fully customizable island 
- They can play separately or visit each其他's islands online 
- No conflicts over design choices 
- Much more flexibility 

So technically, the user is correct. The girlfriend's request doesn't make sense because " sharing one village" on one Switch means they'd be forced to cohabitate in the same save file, which is not how the game is designed for two players. The standard way to " play together" in Animal Crossing is each having their own save on their own console, then using online features to visit. 

The girlfriend's " sense of togetherness" is misdirected. True togetherness in this context would be visiting each其他's islands online, not being forced to share the same physical space. In fact, sharing one save file would likely cause more conflicts ( " why did you cut down my tree?") rather than less.

Wait no - actually, on one Switch, you can have multiple user accounts, but each user account can only have one Animal Crossing save. So if they both use the same Switch, they'd each have their own save file on the same console, but... no, that's not right. 

Correction: For Animal Crossing: New Horizons, each save file is tied to a user account on the Switch.
